analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is a stale GC worklist pointer: `incremental_sweep_phase()` can free an entire `mrb_heap_page` (`mrb_free(mrb, page)`) when `dead_slot` is true, but it does not unlink any objects from `gc->gray_list`/`gc->atomic_gray_list` that may still point into that page. Later in the same full-GC cycle, marking (`incremental_marking_phase` -> `gc_mark_children` -> `mrb_gc_mark`) dereferences one of those dangling `RBasic*` entries, producing the heap-use-after-free seen at `mrb_gc_mark` line 743 (`is_white(obj)`).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered by Ruby input that drives GC through both mark/sweep transitions with object graph mutations so that a heap page becomes fully dead and is freed during `incremental_sweep_phase`, while at least one object from that page remains queued in gray/atomic gray lists. In this PoV, `mruby_fuzzer` calls `mrb_load_string` on attacker-controlled script; the script causes heavy allocations/GC activity (including `GC.start` patterns), leading to page reclamation and later mark-phase traversal of stale pointers.
